% Pattern: number/aux. A \label after an equation in a definition takes the
% number of the equation, as the anchor equation.1.1 of the .aux tells, so
% the definition keeps the number 1.2 of the counter and not the 1 of the
% label. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1.1
% want definition-1 definition 1.2
% want lemma-1 statement/lemma 1.3
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{definition}[theorem]{Definition}
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\begin{document}
\section{One}
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:first} Every finite space is compact. \end{theorem}
\begin{definition}
A space is fine when
\begin{equation}
a = b
\end{equation}
\label{def:fine}
\end{definition}
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:last} Every point is closed. \end{lemma}
\end{document}
